data.targetWord: A proposed explanation for what is observed, which must be testable by evidence

examples.en-GB: A hypothesis is the starting point of a scientific investigation — it is a testable prediction.

data.targetWord: A well-tested, evidence-based explanation for observed phenomena — not a guess, but one of the strongest types of scientific knowledge

examples.en-GB: The theory of evolution and the theory of gravity are both well-supported scientific theories, not guesses.

data.targetWord: A question about meaning, purpose, or ultimate reality that cannot be answered by scientific evidence alone, such as 'Why is there something rather than nothing?'

examples.en-GB: Science answers how the universe formed, but 'why does it exist at all?' is an ultimate question.

data.targetWord: The leading scientific explanation for the origin of the universe: a rapid expansion from an extremely hot, dense point approximately 13.8 billion years ago

examples.en-GB: The Big Bang theory is supported by evidence such as cosmic microwave background radiation.

data.targetWord: The scientific theory that all life on Earth shares common ancestors and diversified over millions of years through natural selection

examples.en-GB: Evolution is supported by the fossil record, DNA analysis, and comparative anatomy.

data.targetWord: The mechanism of evolution: individuals with advantageous variations are more likely to survive, reproduce, and pass on their traits

examples.en-GB: Natural selection explains how species gradually change to better suit their environments over generations.

data.targetWord: Reading a sacred text as factually true exactly as written, treating it as a historical or scientific account

examples.en-GB: A literal interpretation of Genesis holds that creation happened in six actual 24-hour days.

data.targetWord: Reading a sacred text as conveying deeper theological truths through metaphor, poetry, or allegory rather than as a literal factual account

examples.en-GB: A symbolic interpretation sees the 'six days' of Genesis as representing vast periods or theological meaning.

data.targetWord: The view that evolution is the mechanism God used to create life; science and religious belief are fully compatible

examples.en-GB: Theistic evolution is accepted by the Catholic Church and many mainstream Christian, Muslim, and Jewish scientists.

data.targetWord: The belief that the universe and life were created by God as literally described in sacred texts, often rejecting scientific accounts of origins

examples.en-GB: Young Earth Creationism holds that the Earth is around 6,000 years old, in conflict with scientific dating.

data.targetWord: The view that science and religion can coexist because they address different types of questions — 'how' versus 'why'

examples.en-GB: Many scientists are religious and hold that science and faith are fully compatible.

data.targetWord: The view that God does not exist; atheists generally accept scientific accounts of the universe without a divine explanation

examples.en-GB: An atheist accepts the Big Bang theory and evolution as complete explanations without needing a creator.

data.targetWord: The view that whether God exists is unknown or unknowable; agnostics neither affirm nor deny God's existence

examples.en-GB: An agnostic may accept scientific findings while remaining uncertain about whether God exists.

data.targetWord: A non-religious philosophy emphasising human reason, wellbeing, and ethics; humanists accept scientific findings and base morality on empathy rather than religion

examples.en-GB: Humanists accept evolution and the Big Bang without reference to a creator God.

data.targetWord: The first book of the Hebrew Bible and Christian Old Testament, containing an account of creation in six days that religious traditions interpret in different ways

examples.en-GB: Some Christians read Genesis literally; others read it as theological poetry expressing who created and why.

data.targetWord: Observations and data collected through testing that support or challenge a scientific hypothesis

examples.en-GB: The fossil record is evidence that supports the theory of evolution by natural selection.

data.targetWord: The argument that the complexity of life requires a designer, rather than being explainable by evolution alone; not accepted as science by scientific consensus

examples.en-GB: Intelligent Design is held by some religious believers but is not considered a scientific theory.

data.targetWord: A figure of speech in which something is described as something else to convey a deeper meaning, rather than being intended literally

examples.en-GB: 'The Lord is my shepherd' is a metaphor — it is not a claim about sheep.

data.targetWord: The religious belief that the universe was brought into existence by God, expressing that existence is intentional, purposeful, and good

examples.en-GB: The Genesis creation account expresses that God made the world and saw it was 'very good'.

data.targetWord: The scientific process of sharing findings with other experts who check and challenge them before they are accepted

examples.en-GB: Peer review ensures that scientific findings are checked and cannot rely on a single person's authority.

data.sentence: In science, a well-tested, evidence-based explanation for observed phenomena is called a ____.
The leading scientific explanation for the origin of the universe is called the ____ theory.
The scientific theory that all life on Earth shares common ancestors and diversified through natural selection is called ____.
The mechanism of evolution — where individuals with advantageous traits are more likely to survive and reproduce — is called ____ selection.
Reading a sacred text as conveying deeper truths through metaphor rather than as a literal historical account is called ____ interpretation.
Reading a sacred text as factually true exactly as written is called ____ interpretation.
The view that evolution is the mechanism God used to create life is called ____ evolution.
The view that God does not exist is called ____.
The view that whether God exists is unknown or unknowable is called ____.
The view that science and religion address different questions and can coexist is called ____.
Questions about meaning, purpose, or ultimate reality that science cannot directly answer are called ____ questions.
A non-religious philosophy that bases ethics on human reason and empathy rather than God is called ____.
The first book of the Bible, containing the account of creation in six days, is called ____.
A proposed testable explanation for what is observed in science is called a ____.
The scientific process of sharing findings with other experts who check and challenge them is called ____ review.

data.title: Put the steps in the scientific method in the correct order
items: Observe a phenomenon in the natural world
Form a hypothesis — a testable explanation
Test the hypothesis through experiments and collect evidence
Share findings for peer review and revise or confirm the theory

data.title: Place these events in the history of the universe in the correct order according to the Big Bang theory
items: The Big Bang — rapid expansion from an extremely hot, dense point (~13.8 billion years ago)
First atoms form as the universe cools (~380,000 years after Big Bang)
First stars and galaxies form (~1 billion years after Big Bang)
Our solar system and Earth form (~4.6 billion years ago)

data.title: Arrange these interpretations of Genesis from most literal to most symbolic
items: Young Earth Creationism — six actual 24-hour days; Earth is around 6,000 years old
Day-age theory — each 'day' represents a geological era of millions of years
Framework interpretation — the structure of days is a literary device, not a sequence of events
Purely allegorical reading — Genesis conveys theological truths about God as creator, with no historical claims
